goal: Send a request while a run slot is busy; then free capacity
expected_outcome: Acknowledgement follows durable commit; queued is not running; reaction receipt avoids a redundant text acknowledgement; reaction failure falls back to text; a queue wait over 30 seconds gets one observed queue-depth notice; waiting has a reason and does not trigger a hung-run warning

goal: Start a Codex turn in a forum topic
expected_outcome: Typing stays in the correct topic, continues through a long active call within its inactivity bound, follows section 12's rate bound and stops on wait/cancel/terminal state; its timer/failure never extends a deadline, creates work or blocks a final reply

goal: Emit factual tool/task progress, a stall and subsequent recovery
expected_outcome: Coalesced status reflects evidence; incident notices deduplicate across restart; no raw secrets/reasoning; a reset timer alone cannot claim recovery; final/question/failure is not starved by edits

goal: Spawn a Codex process that never emits an event
expected_outcome: First-event watch still fires within the configured bound; request becomes recoverable/failed with notice; slot and process resources are released or fenced

goal: Run a chatty model, a quiet tool and compaction
expected_outcome: Runtime events renew inactivity; timers do not. No fixed turn-duration or call cap; stop and inactivity preserve completed findings and report unconfirmed effects without replay (§5, §7)

goal: Fill the normal queue, then issue authorized stop/status/reset
expected_outcome: Control remains responsive within budgets; generation blocks stale effects/replies; old receipts remain queryable; revoked/unknown actor gets no effect or reply; reset does not recreate or lose active TaskQ work

goal: Deliver native events and a candidate tool call
expected_outcome: No partial/invalid effect; no guessed success; optional diagnostic can be ignored safely; explicit failed/uncertain outcome retains evidence; typed tools retain the verified effect boundary; native tools use §5 service-user authority and no automatic replay

goal: Provider or transport fails during a request
expected_outcome: Auth/quota/transport reasons differ; no busy loop or billed-key fallback; one logical-operation budget survives restart; server wait honored; stale authorization rechecked before resumed effects

goal: Resume a thread after subscription credentials expire
expected_outcome: Explicit required-login state; refresh does not discard conversation; different account binding is not adopted silently; old effects are reconciled before continuation; live entitlement/renewal is a separate release check

goal: Start with a pinned Codex and a reviewed Telegram manifest
expected_outcome: Component readiness shows the precise missing prerequisite; no unsafe executable admission; remaining read-only status is honest; actual model-visible tools match the reviewed inventory; mocks do not establish production entitlement

goal: Final answer needs several messages with Unicode and code blocks
expected_outcome: Stable persisted text/chunk IDs; receipt-aware ordered continuation; only ambiguous chunks risk bounded duplicates; formatting fallback preserves meaning; no model/tool rerun or false delivered state

goal: Queue slow progress edits and then a terminal result
expected_outcome: Final revision cannot be overwritten; replacement stays in the same authorized route; superseded cosmetic work drops without dropping the final result or regenerating it

goal: Serve DM, ordinary group, General and named forum topics
expected_outcome: Identity/routing preserved; delivery is held with an actionable incident; no fallback to wider chat or private DM; administrative remap is explicit and does not change the original effect authority

goal: Interleave text, album parts, edits and replies from two people/topics
expected_outcome: Each admitted input remains accounted for; bounded assembly preserves author/route/revision; no cross-person merge or swallowed text; unsupported content gets an explicit outcome only for authorized senders

goal: Plan restart/update with accepted input, a running manager and pending output
expected_outcome: Persisted work survives; stale descendants are terminated/fenced; original pending requests reconcile; no startup backlog discard; TaskQ worker continues under TaskQ ownership; new readiness follows recovery checks

goal: Persist work, then lose its timer/event notification
expected_outcome: Periodic scan recovers work without a user nudge; dirty key reruns once; one failing key does not block others; no duplicate create/effect/delivery obligation; external call does not hold the DB transaction

goal: Run deadlines/backoff, then change wall clock and restart
expected_outcome: Monotonic live deadlines remain bounded; restart does not reset attempts or grant unlimited extra run time; invalid time evidence is explicit rather than healthy

goal: Independently break ingress, dispatch, model, delivery and the service process
expected_outcome: Correct component becomes stale/unknown; external monitor detects total service failure; no claim of successful Telegram alert when delivery is down; recovery notice requires fresh evidence; no alert/restart storm

goal: Stress one route and resource budgets during another normal conversation
expected_outcome: Bounds and fair service hold; uncommitted input is not acknowledged; raw secrets/message bodies do not leak into diagnostics; resources/child handles are released; telemetry failure does not block the core flow

goal: Upgrade a pinned PilotQ/Codex/config/schema set with accepted work, then roll back
expected_outcome: Current/previous version and compatibility are explicit; incompatible downgrade stops safely; receipts and native mappings survive compatible rollback; restored effects reconcile with TaskQ; actual Linux service and storage proof is separate from fake traces
